crime: Early that evening in the lounge, {WITCH_NAME} projected a moon knight performing a string of pratfalls for a girl. The girl laughed and lingered to keep her company. Then she admitted she had only laughed to be polite and refused to stay for that night’s voyage to the moon.

{WITCH_NAME} plunged a sword into her chest, killing her. She called a prisoner for help and, when the prisoner arrived, projected a masked assailant fleeing with the sword. The prisoner took the figure for the fleeing murderer and threw a cup to stop it. The cup passed straight through its torso.

At the trial court, the prisoner’s account turned on that impossible passage: the masked fugitive had no body. The figure was a decoy {WITCH_NAME} had projected to fake the killer’s escape for the very witness she had summoned.
fields.epitaph: She leaves her imagined worlds behind—each a home with no one in it.
execution: The execution stand binds her to a marionette frame with tethers around her neck and limbs. The frame hoists her by the noose around her neck and jerks her into a cruel, comic jig. She struggles as it works her body through the dance. Even after she stops responding, it keeps jerking her dangling limbs until her head hangs limp.

magic.name: Waking Worlds
magic.text: She can project scenes from her imagination into the space around her as shared, three-dimensional sights and sounds.
